title: Unix Epoch Clock
intro: This clock displays the signed count of ordinary Unix seconds since 00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970.
structure: The reading is one signed decimal integer rather than hours, minutes and seconds. Zero denotes the epoch; positive values follow it and negative values precede it. Each day in the numerical Unix model contributes 86400 seconds.
example: At the epoch the reading is 0; one second later it is 1; one second before it is -1. At 00:00 UTC on 2 January 1970 it is 86400. An instant one microsecond before the epoch also reads -1, because the provider floors negative fractions rather than truncating toward zero.
history: Unix epoch notation is a modern computer time coordinate, distinct from traditional wall-clock or calendar displays.
model: The provider floor-divides the signed native microsecond instant by 1000000, preserving the sign and rounding toward negative infinity. It formats the quotient as a decimal integer. Scheduling uses a positive subsecond remainder and rounds the wait to the next whole second upward to milliseconds.
limits: Locale, local offset, coordinates, seconds toggle and vertical display flag do not alter the integer reading. The model follows Unix seconds rather than a leap-second-aware elapsed atomic-time count; it does not impose a 32-bit signed timestamp limit.
